THE BUREAU’S SURVIVAL GUIDE

Don’t get
reeled in.

  1. Break the rush.

    Threats and tight deadlines can push you to act without checking. Pause before replying or paying.

  2. Take your own route.

    Open the company’s known app or website yourself. Ask support to confirm the request.

  3. Keep secrets secret.

    Never send passwords, PINs, or one-time codes in a message reply.

Already clicked or shared something? ↗

Stop interacting. Change exposed passwords through the real service and enable multi-factor authentication. If money or payment details are involved, contact your bank promptly using its official number. Report the message through official support.

Guidance: FTC phishing guide ↗. Warnings are clues, not proof.
WELCOME TO YOUR NEW DESK

A little suspicious?

  1. Pick a case.

    Flag it or choose no obvious red flags. Learn why, then open the next file.
